messages:
Ava (Design): quick one — working on the Model Latency view. Thinking of replacing the current histogram+box with a compact density overlay + dot-outlier markers. Thoughts on readability vs precise quantiles?
Miguel (Eng): overlay looks cleaner when you have many models, but can hide multi-modality. Maybe toggle between 'density' and 'quantiles' view? :thinking_face: 
Priya (PM): toggles sound good. Also we need clear units — current header says "latency" but some folks asked whether to show "ms" or "milliseconds". short vs verbose?
Connor (ML): for engineering teams I prefer "ms" (compact) but make hover show full label e.g., "milliseconds" and exact value. Also, smoothing parameter matters — default too high flattens spikes. Suggest default smoothing=0.6 and a small UI slider for advanced users.
Ava (Design): agree on slider. UI idea: a small "Smoothing" microcontrol (0.0–1.0) next to the chart. If user sets custom smoothing, we store it per-user.
Sam (A11y): small note — density overlays rely on color fill. We must ensure pattern or accessible stroke options for colorblind users and ensure contrast meets AA for chart foreground text. Also keyboard users need meaningful focus states on dots/tooltips.
Miguel (Eng): good call. Implementation questions: what do we do about extreme outliers? Right now extreme requests ( >10s) stretch the axis. Options: clamp the x-axis to 99th percentile and show a "+N outliers" indicator, OR use a log scale toggle.
Priya (PM): clamp to 99th + indicator seems more user-friendly; log scale is accurate but surprising for non-technical users. We could add an advanced toggle for log scale.
Connor (ML): for alerting we should still compute quantiles on raw values (not clamped). So when users click "99th" in the legend, it should reflect true 99th of the full data. UI clamp is purely display.
Ava (Design): UX copy: Legend item should read "p50 / p95 / p99" with microcopy on hover like "Median / 95th percentile / 99th percentile (raw)". Use short labels on chart to reduce clutter.
Sam (A11y): microcopy must be available to screen readers, not only hover. Use aria-describedby linking to hidden text.
Miguel (Eng): prototype snippet for clamping + outlier count (pseudo):
```
const displayLimit = percentile(data, 0.99);
const visible = data.filter(d => d <= displayLimit);
const outliers = data.length - visible.length;
renderAxis(max(visible));
renderOutlierBadge(`+${outliers} outliers > ${displayLimit}ms`);
```
Ava (Design): looks good — can we make badge clickable to expand to full range? UX: badge toggles "show all" and opens a small modal explaining why we clamped.
Priya (PM): keep default collapsed but remember user's choice per-session. Also add a tooltip copy: "Displaying up to the 99th percentile by default — click to show full range."
Connor (ML): one more: smoothing + KDE bandwidth should respect sample size. When sample < 50, disable smoothing and show raw bars to avoid misleading shapes.
Ava (Design): noted — we should add a tiny helper: "Low sample: raw data shown" when <50.
Sam (A11y): final check: keyboard-only tooltip access, ARIA labels for legend toggles, and ensure color contrast. I can run the a11y checklist once prototype is up.
DesignBot: Reminder — please add an item to the design backlog: "Latency chart — density overlay, smoothing control, outlier clamping + badge, accessible legend labels". @Ava (Design) assigned. :white_check_mark:
Ava (Design): thanks! I'll push a mock and link it here tomorrow.
